# Brim

> Brim is a free, open-source macOS menu bar app for Apple Silicon Macs (macOS 14 or newer). It lets one person run several Claude Code accounts on the same Mac (per-account usage, automatic account picking, moving a conversation to another account when one hits its usage limit), ends leftover development processes when memory is tight, and bundles a system monitor, Port Manager, Kill Process, Cleaner, Uninstaller, Homebrew manager, app updates, clipboard history, keep awake and a Dynamic Island. Written in Swift, licensed GPL-3.0-or-later, built by Eliseo Robles (Robles Consulting LLC), and based on Vorssaint.

Key facts:

- Price: free. No account, no telemetry, no analytics, no subscription.
- Platform: macOS 14 Sonoma or newer, Apple Silicon (M1 or later) only. No Intel support.
- Install: build from source with `BRIM_SIGN_IDENTITY=- ./build.sh --dev --install` (Xcode Command Line Tools; no Xcode project, no dependencies).
- Claude Code accounts: each account has its own Claude Code config folder (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, for example `~/.claude-work`), signed in once by Claude Code itself through a private browser window. Brim never reads, copies or refreshes a Claude credential.
- Shell commands: `claude` starts on the account whose weekly limit renews soonest; `cc <account>` starts on a named account; `cx` (after `/exit`) continues the latest conversation on another account, `cx --to <account>` on a named one. Every account folder holds a copy of every conversation, so `/resume` works on any account.
- Usage: each account's weekly limit, model-specific limits and renewal times in the menu bar and a Claude Code status line.
- MCP: every MCP server is on everywhere by default and can be switched off per repo; repo-only servers are supported.
- Memory module: lists leftover dev process groups (dev servers, test runners, watchers whose editor or terminal is gone) and apps unused for hours; levels Inform, Notify and Automatic (automatic only while memory is tight); a runaway brake for processes whose footprint explodes; detects the macOS fseventsd memory leak.
- Not affiliated with Anthropic. Claude and Claude Code are trademarks of Anthropic.
- Not related to brimdata's Brim network-analysis app (now called Zui) or to Brim Financial.
